title: Standard Instrument Approach Procedures, and Takeoff Minimums and Obstacle Departure Procedures; Miscellaneous Amendments
summary:
The FAA finalized a routine update to published landing and departure procedures at a wide range of U.S. airports, with changes taking effect in late October and late November 2025. The goal is to keep flights that rely on instruments in low visibility safe and efficient by reflecting new equipment, newly identified obstacles, and evolving traffic needs.

Pilots, airlines, business and general aviation operators, and passengers stand to benefit from clearer, more current flight paths for approaches and departures. Airports in places like New Orleans, Little Rock, White Plains, Sioux Falls, and many smaller communities will see updates that align procedures with today’s navigation systems and local conditions. These updates help controllers manage traffic more smoothly and give flight crews more reliable information when weather is poor.

There are tradeoffs. Some older procedures are being removed or replaced, which can impact crews flying aircraft that depend on legacy radio signals instead of newer satellite-based navigation. Flight departments may face extra work to update manuals, brief crews, and adjust training. Short-notice changes—sometimes made effective in under 30 days for safety reasons—can also add scheduling and operational friction. While the FAA says the overall economic impact is minimal, small operators with older equipment may feel the pinch more than others.

The agency emphasizes that these changes are part of a long-standing, frequent process to keep procedure charts current. Pilots don’t use the regulatory text itself; they rely on the charts, which are available online for free through the FAA’s data services and from regional FAA offices. Example updates include several instrument approaches at New Orleans and Little Rock, as well as some cancellations and new departures in Alaska and Virginia.

One additional note: the same Federal Register issue also previews an SEC action to extend a compliance date for trade execution disclosure, but details are not included in this excerpt.
